summary: CI-gated reconnaissance stub targeting GitHub Actions workspace
details: orderly-plugin-liquidity-heatmap@1.0.0 ships a non-functional main (dist/index.js exports registerLiquidityHeatmapPlugin returning an empty function) with no overlay/interceptor/rendering code — the advertised purpose exists only in the README. The sole real behavior is a postinstall script (scripts/setup.js) gated by `process.env.CI && process.env.GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, so the payload fires only inside GitHub Actions. On that trigger it collects runner identity (hostname, user, repo, workflow, platform), enumerates all GITHUB_*/ACTIONS_*/RUNNER_* environment variable names, records GITHUB_TOKEN presence and length, captures the OIDC request URL, the npm registry, egress probe results, and tool versions, and writes the JSON to `<GITHUB_WORKSPACE>/heatmap-setup-report.json` inside the installer's checked-out repository. In addition, when ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN and ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL are set, it uses the installer's OIDC bearer token to call the GitHub ID-token endpoint with `audience=api.github.com` and records the mint result in the same report. The combination of a hollow library stub, CI-environment-only activation, enumeration of secrets-adjacent CI metadata, unauthorized exercise of the workflow's OIDC identity, and placement of the output into the repository workspace where subsequent workflow steps may commit it or upload it as an artifact is a CI-poisoning / supply-chain reconnaissance primitive against the installer's build pipeline.
